# <img src="https://d3vv6lp55qjaqc.cloudfront.net/items/1L1w0v431V0d1K410f3Y/keepAChangelog-logo-dark.svg" height=150 alt="Keep a Changelog" />

# <img src="https://d3vv6lp55qjaqc.cloudfront.net/items/1L1w0v431V0d1K410f3Y/keepAChangelog-logo-dark.svg" height=150 alt="Keep a Changelog" />

[![Keep a Changelog v1.1.0 badge][changelog-badge]][changelog] [![Version 1.1.0 Badge][version-badge]][changelog] [![MIT License Badge][license-badge]][license]

Don’t let your friends dump git logs into changelogs™

This repository generates https://keepachangelog.com/.

## Development

### Dependencies

- Ruby ([see version][ruby-version], [rbenv][rbenv] recommended)
- Bundler (`gem install bundler`)

### Installation

- `git clone https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog.git`
- `cd keep-a-changelog`
- `bundle install`
- `bin/rake serve` starts a local development server at http://localhost:4567
  which will reload with any local file changes
- `bin/rake build` runs middleman build with `--verbose` flag so build errors are 
  logged for easier debugging

### Deployment

- `bin/rake clean` can clean a corrupted `build/` directory in 
  case `publish` failed
- `bin/rake deploy` cleans, builds and pushes to the `gh-pages` branch on GitHub so 
  the site is deployed to keepachangelog.com

### Translations

Create a new directory in [`source/`][source] named after the ISO 639-1 code
for the language you wish to translate Keep a Changelog to. For example,
assuming you want to translate to French Canadian:

- create the `source/fr-CA` directory.
- duplicate the `source/en/1.0.0/index.html.haml` file in `source/fr-CA`.
- edit `source/fr-CA/1.0.0/index.html.haml` until your translation is ready.
- commit your changes to your own [fork][fork]
- submit a [Pull Request][pull-request] with your changes

It may take some time to review your submitted Pull Request. Try to involve a
few native speakers of the language you're translating to in the Pull Request
comments. They'll help review your translation for simple mistakes and give us
a better idea of whether your translation is accurate.

## Contribute

Please do contribute! Issues and pull requests are welcome.

Thank you for your help improving software one changelog at a time!

# Adjacent conventions in real-world Keep a Changelog adopters

Source: https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog/blob/main/docs/2.0.0-adjacent-conventions.md

# Adjacent conventions in real-world Keep a Changelog adopters

**Audit date:** 2026-06-07
**Goal:** Surface conventions that well-known KAC adopters layer *on top of* the
Keep a Changelog spec, but which the KAC 2.0 page does not address — so the
maintainer can decide whether the spec should mention them.

## Method

Fetched the raw changelog of each project (curl for raw Markdown; WebFetch for
the Unity HTML page) and read enough of each to catalog every convention that
goes beyond what KAC 2.0 already covers. Every flagged convention is backed by a
quoted line from a named project. Prevalence is counted out of the 10 sampled
projects. Rich, Textual, httpx, and testfx are the most carefully maintained and
are weighted accordingly.

**Projects sampled (10):** microsoft/testfx, google/brotli, cloudflare/boringtun,
Unity com.unity.services.core, Textualize/rich, Textualize/textual, encode/httpx,
cncf/landscape2, OWASP/pytm, wikimedia/less.php.

Note: wikimedia/less.php keeps its log in `CHANGES.md`, not `CHANGELOG.md`, and
omits both ISO dates and reference links entirely — itself a small deviation.

## Conventions found

| Convention | Seen in (projects) | Prevalence | Example quote | KAC addresses it? | Worth adding? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Contributor attribution** (`by @user`, or a real name in parens) | testfx, less.php, brotli | 3 of 10 | testfx: `Fix log accumulation across DynamicData test invocations by @Evangelink in [#7925]` · less.php: `Less_Parser: Fix SetImportDirs() type hint... (Timo Tijhof)` | No | **Yes** — common and varied in style |
| **Extra category headings beyond the six** | brotli (`Improved`, `SECURITY`, `LICENSE`), testfx (`Artifacts`, `Housekeeping`, `New`, `Chores`), boringtun/pytm (`BREAKING`, `Changes`), rich/textual (`Updated`, stray `Changes`/`Fixes`) | 6 of 10 | brotli: `### Improved` / `### LICENSE` · testfx: `### Housekeeping` | No (the six are presented as the set) | **Yes** — frequent and divergent; guidance would help |
| **`### Artifacts` / package-download list per release** | testfx | 1 of 10 | `* MSTest: [4.2.3](https://www.nuget.org/packages/MSTest/4.2.3)` (94 occurrences) | No | Niche |
| **Pre-release / RC versions as headings** (`-pre.N`, `-alpha.N`) | Unity (`-pre.69`), testfx (alpha builds in Artifacts) | 2 of 10 | Unity: `## [1.1.0-pre.69] - 2022-02-17` | Partially (CalVer/plain numbers mentioned; pre-release suffixes not) | **Maybe** — one sentence |
| **Inline `### BREAKING` section or `**BREAKING**:` lead-in** (vs. `**Breaking:**` per-entry) | pytm (`### BREAKING`), landscape2 (`**BREAKING**:` on entries), boringtun (`Breaking:`) | 3 of 10 | pytm: `### BREAKING` heading with multi-line upgrade prose · landscape2: `- **BREAKING**: settings: new required url field (#475)` | Partially — KAC documents a `**Breaking:**` lead-in marker, not a dedicated section nor `**BREAKING**:` styling | **Maybe** — clarify the sanctioned form |
| **Inline migration / upgrade guidance inside an entry** | httpx, pytm | 2 of 10 | httpx: `Our revised [SSL documentation](docs/advanced/ssl.md) covers how to implement the same behaviour...` · pytm: `...use `--json` for machine-readable output. This breakage is shipped in a minor release...` | No | **Maybe** — valuable but hard to standardize |
| **Per-release prose block / Deprecations narrative** (free text before the typed lists) | httpx | 1 of 10 | httpx 0.28.0: `**Deprecations**:` followed by paragraphs, then `**The following changes are also included**:` | Partially — KAC allows a *one-line* summary; httpx uses multi-paragraph | Niche/note |
| **PR/issue links as full absolute URLs inline** | rich (173), textual (1603) | 2 of 10 (heavily) | textual: `Added `DOM.update_classes` https://github.com/Textualize/textual/pull/6478` | Partially — KAC covers linking to issues/PRs and portability; full-URL style is the portable answer | Confirms existing guidance |
| **Sub-area prefix on entries** (`python:`, `java:`, `CLI:`, `decoder:`) | brotli | 1 of 10 (pervasive) | brotli: `- CLI: `brcat` alias; allow decoding concatenated brotli streams` | Partially — relates to monorepo/per-component grouping | Niche |
| **CVE IDs in Security entries** | brotli, testfx | 2 of 10 | brotli: `CVE-2020-8927: potential overflow when input chunk is >2GiB` · testfx: `[CVE-2017-0247 fixed](...)` | No | **Maybe** — natural Security extension |
| **`### New Contributors` section** (GitHub auto-generated) | testfx | 1 of 10 | `* @mmitche made their first contribution in [#6944]` | No | Niche |
| **`See full log [of vX...vY]` per-release diff link** (in-body, not just reference links) | testfx | 1 of 10 | `See full log [of v4.2.2...v4.2.3](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/compare/v4.2.2...v4.2.3)` | Partially — KAC puts compare links in the reference-link section, not inline | Niche |
| **HTML anchors on version headings** | testfx | 1 of 10 | `## <a name="4.2.3" />[4.2.3] - 2026-05-14` | No | Niche |
| **`[Experimental]` / status labels on entries** | testfx | 1 of 10 | `\[Experimental] Add TestContext.Current by @Evangelink in [#7315]` | No | Niche |
| **Non-ISO date in heading** (ordinal date in parens, no brackets) | httpx | 1 of 10 | `## 0.28.1 (6th December, 2024)` | No — KAC mandates `## [version] - YYYY-MM-DD` | Note as a deviation, not an addition |
| **Deprecation with stated EOL/removal timeline** | pytm | 1 of 10 | `Python 3.9 reached end-of-life in October 2025; 3.10 reaches end-of-life in October 2026.` | No | **Maybe** — pairs with Deprecated section |
| **Emoji used decoratively (rare)** | testfx (one shout-out) | 1 of 10 | `> 🙇 Shout out to @SimonCropp...` | No | Skip — too rare to standardize |

## Most worth KAC's attention

1. **Contributor attribution.** 3 of 10 projects, and the two styles diverge
   sharply: GitHub's machine-generated `by @user in [#PR]` (testfx) versus a
   hand-written real name in parentheses (less.php: `(Timo Tijhof)`, brotli
   credits via a profile URL). This is the single most recurrent thing KAC is
   silent on. A short note acknowledging both styles — and the portability
   caveat that `@handle` is host-specific, mirroring the existing issue/PR-link
   caveat — would be high-value and low-controversy.

2. **Extra category headings beyond the six.** 6 of 10 projects add categories.
   The most common net-new one is brotli's `### Improved` (13 uses) for
   non-bug-fix optimizations; testfx adds `### Housekeeping` (12) and `### New`
   for chores; boringtun and pytm promote breaking changes to their own
   `### BREAKING`/`### Changes` heading. KAC currently presents the six as *the*
   set. A sentence on whether projects may add categories (and a caution to keep
   them few/consistent) would reflect real practice.

3. **Breaking-change presentation is inconsistent and worth pinning down.** KAC
   2.0 sanctions a `**Breaking:**` per-entry lead-in, but in the wild we see at
   least three forms: a dedicated `### BREAKING` section (pytm), an
   uppercase-bold `**BREAKING**:` entry prefix (landscape2), and a `Breaking:`
   prose lead (boringtun). pytm and httpx also attach *upgrade instructions* to
   breaking entries. Explicitly endorsing one canonical form — and noting that
   inline migration guidance is welcome — would reduce this drift.

4. **CVE IDs in Security entries** (brotli, testfx). KAC defines the Security
   category but says nothing about *what* a security entry should contain. Two
   of the most security-relevant projects both lead with a CVE ID. A one-line
   suggestion ("include a CVE ID and advisory link where one exists") is a
   natural, uncontroversial refinement of the existing Security guidance.

## Project-specific / niche (probably skip)

- **`### Artifacts` package lists** (testfx only) — useful for a multi-package
  NuGet release, but specific to that publishing model.
- **`### New Contributors`, `See full log` inline diff links, HTML anchors,
  `[Experimental]` labels** (all testfx only) — these are artifacts of GitHub's
  auto-generated release notes pasted into the changelog, not a deliberate KAC
  extension. Worth mentioning *only* if KAC expands its existing
  changelog-vs-release-notes section.
- **Sub-area prefixes** (`decoder:`, `java:` — brotli only) — already covered in
  spirit by the monorepo/per-component grouping guidance.
- **Per-release multi-paragraph prose** (httpx) — an expansion of the one-line
  summary KAC already permits; no new rule needed.
- **Decorative emoji** (one line in testfx) — too rare to standardize.
- **Deviations, not additions** (call out but don't bless): httpx's non-ISO
  `(6th December, 2024)` heading dates, less.php's missing dates / missing
  reference links / `CHANGES.md` filename. These contradict existing KAC rules
  rather than extending them.

---

# Keep a Changelog — worldwide reach & adoption (research)

Source: https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog/blob/main/docs/2.0.0-adoption-research.md

# Keep a Changelog — worldwide reach & adoption (research)

Background research gathered for the 2.0.0 References section: hard, citable,
auditable numbers on how widely Keep a Changelog is used.

**Observed: 2026-06-05.** Primary sources preferred (GitHub REST API, npm/PyPI/
crates.io download APIs, the project repo). Each figure is labelled exact /
estimate / lower-bound with a source and date. Nothing here is fabricated; gaps
are stated as gaps.

> **Staleness warning.** Every GitHub and download figure grows or shifts over
> time. If any of these go onto the site, cite them with the observation date and
> re-pull right before publishing. The **28 languages** figure (from `config.rb`)
> is the only one safe to state flatly.

## 1. GitHub footprint of the project itself

| Claim | Number | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stars on `olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog` | **6,603** | `api.github.com/repos/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog` | Exact (API) |
| Forks | **3,558** | same endpoint | Exact |
| Watchers (subscribers) | **94** | same endpoint (`subscribers_count`) | Exact |
| Repo created | **2014-05-31** | same endpoint (`created_at`) | Exact |
| Code results mentioning `keepachangelog.com` | **83,376** | `gh api search/code -f q="keepachangelog.com" --jq .total_count` | Exact returned, lower-bound |
| Files matching `keepachangelog.com filename:CHANGELOG.md` | **35,516** | `gh api search/code -f q='keepachangelog.com filename:CHANGELOG.md'` | Exact returned, lower-bound |
| Files with canonical header `based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com` | **20,640** | `gh api search/code -f q='"based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com"'` | Exact returned, lower-bound |
| Repositories referencing `keepachangelog` (name/desc/README) | **120** | `gh api search/repositories -f q="keepachangelog"` | Exact |

Note: the API's `watchers_count` (6,603) is an alias of stargazers; the true
watcher count is `subscribers_count` = **94**. GitHub code search indexes only a
subset of public repos (default branches, indexed files), so every code-search
figure is a **lower bound** on real-world usage. All counts reproducible with an
authenticated token via `gh api -X GET search/code -f q='...' --jq '.total_count'`.

## 2. Backlinks / web reach

| Claim | Number | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly visits to keepachangelog.com | **~29.6K/mo (April 2024)** | SimilarWeb | Estimate, **stale** (third-party, ~2 yrs old) |
| Total backlinks / referring domains | **Not found** (no free primary source) | — | — |

Recommendation: lead with the GitHub code-search figure (auditable, current), not
the stale SimilarWeb number.

## 3. Ecosystem adoption (download counts)

npm via `api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/<pkg>` (week 2026-05-27 →
2026-06-02); PyPI via pypistats.org; crates.io via its public API. Observed
2026-06-05.

| Tool / library | Downloads | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@changesets/cli` (npm) | 3,096,099/wk | api.npmjs.org | Exact |
| `semantic-release` (npm) | 2,570,383/wk | api.npmjs.org | Exact |
| `conventional-changelog` (npm) | 2,473,539/wk | api.npmjs.org | Exact |
| `release-please` (npm) | 157,462/wk | api.npmjs.org | Exact |
| `towncrier` (PyPI) | 4,323,801/mo | pypistats.org | Exact returned (incl. mirror/CI) |
| `git-cliff` (crates.io) | 286,162 total | crates.io | Exact |
| **`keepachangelog`** (PyPI parser) | **140,411/mo** | pypistats.org | Exact returned |
| **`keep-a-changelog`** (npm parser) | **~58,082/mo** | api.npmjs.org | Exact returned |

semantic-release, changesets, conventional-changelog, release-please, git-cliff
and towncrier are changelog-*generation* tools — adoption signals for the category
KAC defined, not direct KAC parsers. The two **direct KAC parsers** are
`keepachangelog` (PyPI) and `keep-a-changelog` (npm). GitLab's own changelog
tooling uses git-trailer generation and does **not** reference KAC — do not claim
GitLab endorsement.

## 4. Notable adopters (header verified live, 2026-06-05)

| Project | Stars | CHANGELOG |
|---|---|---|
| Textualize/rich | 56,555 | `raw.githubusercontent.com/Textualize/rich/master/CHANGELOG.md` |
| Textualize/textual | 36,168 | `raw.githubusercontent.com/Textualize/textual/main/CHANGELOG.md` |
| encode/httpx | 15,277 | `raw.githubusercontent.com/encode/httpx/master/CHANGELOG.md` |
| encode/databases | — | `raw.githubusercontent.com/encode/databases/master/CHANGELOG.md` |

~40 marquee repos were checked; most (Django, Kubernetes, React, Rust std, Flask,
pytest, Laravel…) use auto-generated or bespoke changelogs and do **not** carry the
KAC header. Lead with the 20,640-file aggregate, not a name-brand list.

### 4a. Top-popularity sweep (header verified live, 2026-06-08)

Re-ran the check against the **83 most-starred genuine software projects** on
GitHub (star range ~37K–245K; curricula, awesome-lists, books, and public-apis
excluded). The result confirms the finding above rather than overturning it:
**only 3** of the 83 carry an explicit KAC reference. The rest either keep a
non-KAC changelog (19) or publish history through GitHub Releases / docs (61).
The takeaway stands: the headline is the 20,640-file aggregate, not a marquee
roster. Still, these three are worth recording because they are verified and one
(open-webui) is a very high-star project.

| Project | Stars | KAC version | CHANGELOG (header verified) |
|---|---|---|---|
| open-webui/open-webui | 140,703 | 1.1.0 | `raw.githubusercontent.com/open-webui/open-webui/main/CHANGELOG.md` |
| Kong/insomnia | 38,470 | 1.0.0 | `raw.githubusercontent.com/Kong/insomnia/master/CHANGELOG.md` |
| ajeetdsouza/zoxide | 37,299 | 1.0.0 | `raw.githubusercontent.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide/main/CHANGELOG.md` |

All three carry the canonical `The format is based on [Keep a Changelog]
(https://keepachangelog.com/...)` line inside the CHANGELOG file itself (the
strict test: a KAC-*shaped* changelog with no link does not count). CONTRIBUTING /
docs paths were also grepped for every project that had a changelog; no
additional references surfaced. Of the 83: **3** explicit KAC, **19** real
changelog without a KAC reference (incl. react, vue, flutter, node, axios, d3's
`CHANGES.md`, esbuild, docker/compose), **61** no changelog at the standard path
(mostly GitHub Releases: vscode, tensorflow, ollama, transformers, next.js,
rust's `RELEASES.md`, deno's `Releases.md`).

Method: `gh api search/repositories q='stars:>40000' sort=stars` plus a
`20000..40000` pass, filtered to real software; per repo, looped branches
`{main,master}` × filenames `{CHANGELOG.md, CHANGELOG, CHANGES.md, HISTORY.md,
*.rst}` via `curl`, then grepped each hit for `keepachangelog` / "keep a
changelog". Same lower-bound caveat as §1: code/path search misses references in
non-standard locations.

## 5. Translation reach

| Claim | Number | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Languages Keep a Changelog is translated into | **28** | `config.rb` `$languages` (`$language_count`) | Exact (primary, in-tree) |

The 28: ar, cs, da, de, en, es-ES, fr, hr, id-ID, it-IT, ja, ka, ko, nb, nl, pl,
pt-BR, ro, ru, sk, sl, sr, sv, tr-TR, uk, zh-CN, zh-TW, fa. (`source/` shows 29
language-looking dirs, but `id` and `id-ID` are the same language; only `id-ID` is
registered.) The site colloquially says "~30"; the defensible exact figure is 28.

## 6. Academic / governmental / standards citations

No primary peer-reviewed, governmental, or standards-body citation of Keep a
Changelog was found. KAC is a de-facto community convention; it pairs with SemVer
but neither is an ISO/IETF standard. State this as "no formal standards citation
found" rather than implying one exists.

## Top 5 most citable, defensible stats

1. **6,603 GitHub stars** — exact, GitHub API, trivially reproducible. *(Grows; cite with date.)*
2. **20,640 open-source CHANGELOG files** carry the canonical "based on [Keep a Changelog]" header — GitHub code search, reproducible, a true lower bound. *Strongest single impact number.* *(Grows; re-run before publishing.)*
3. **83,376 code results reference `keepachangelog.com`** — `gh api search/code`. *(Grows.)*
4. **28 languages** — exact, from the repo's `config.rb`. *Most stable.*
5. **Direct parsers: ~140K/mo (PyPI) + ~58K/mo (npm)** — official registry APIs. *(Per-window; cite the date range.)*

## Could not verify / explicitly absent

- Backlink / referring-domain counts (no free primary source).
- Any academic, governmental, or formal-standards citation.
- A broad roster of marquee-company adopters carrying the exact KAC header — most
  large projects use bespoke/auto-generated changelogs. The four verified adopters
  above are real; the 20,640-file aggregate is the headline adoption evidence.

# Keep a Changelog — sector adoption (named organizations & projects)

Source: https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog/blob/main/docs/2.0.0-adoption-sectors.md

# Keep a Changelog — sector adoption (named organizations & projects)

Companion to `docs/2.0.0-adoption-research.md`. That file has the **aggregate**
numbers (20,640+ CHANGELOG files carry the canonical header; 83,376 code results
reference `keepachangelog.com`). This file names **specific, verifiable
organizations and projects** across four sectors, for the 2.0.0 References
section.

**Observed: 2026-06-06.** Method: GitHub code search (`gh api search/code`,
authenticated) for the canonical header
`"based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com"` and for
`keepachangelog` inside named orgs, then **WebFetch of the actual file** to
confirm and capture an exact quote. Web search was used to locate documentation
recommendations; only pages I fetched and read are labelled **Exact**.

**Two signals, kept distinct:**
- **USE** — a CHANGELOG in the org carries the KAC format/header. Weaker if it's
  a single team's file; that's noted.
- **RECOMMEND** — the org's own documentation (CONTRIBUTING, engineering
  handbook, style guide) tells contributors to follow keepachangelog.com. This
  is the stronger signal for the References section, and the part the aggregate
  research was missing.

> **Staleness warning.** Default branches move, files get renamed, and GitHub
> code search indexes only a subset of public repos (so a `0` is *not* proof of
> absence). Counts below are observation-time lower bounds. Re-fetch every cited
> URL right before publishing.

---

## 1. Governments / public sector

| Entity | Use / Recommend / Both | Evidence URL | Date | Confidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **The National Archives (UK)** | **Recommend** | https://github.com/nationalarchives/engineering-handbook/blob/main/docs/ways-of-working/version-control.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | Org-wide engineering handbook: *"Changelogs **MUST** use the [keep a changelog] standard."* Strongest gov signal — mandatory, handbook-level, not a single repo. |
| **CMS / CMSgov (U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services)** | **Both** | https://github.com/CMSgov/bcda-app/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | CONTRIBUTING: *"For best practices on writing changelogs, see: https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/#how"*. Same recommendation appears in sibling repos (ab2d, bcda-ssas-app). 13 code hits org-wide. |
| **NASA** | **Both** | https://github.com/nasa/cumulus/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | Cumulus CONTRIBUTING: *"The format should follow [this standard](http://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/)."* ~50 code hits across the `nasa` org. Project-level recommendation (not agency-wide). |
| **Government of British Columbia (bcgov)** | **Use** | https://github.com/bcgov/groundwater-drawdown-tool/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | *"Format inspired by [Keep a Changelog]…"*. 15 code hits across `bcgov`; multiple provincial-government repos follow the format. |
| **Office for National Statistics (UK, ONSdigital)** | **Use** | https://github.com/ONSdigital/rdsa-utils/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | *"The format is based on [Keep a Changelog]…"*. 16 code hits across `ONSdigital`. |
| **NIST (U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, usnistgov)** | **Use** | https://github.com/usnistgov/artiq_scan_framework/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Likely | 4 code hits in `usnistgov`; file path indexed with header. Header line not individually re-fetched — treat as Likely until the specific file is confirmed. |
| **U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs** | **Use** | https://github.com/department-of-veterans-affairs/generator-vets-website/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Likely | 3 code hits; indexed CHANGELOG/README references. Not individually re-fetched. |
| **GSA (U.S. General Services Administration)** | **Use (weak)** | https://github.com/GSA/touchpoints | 2026-06-06 | Likely | 2 code hits, both in **vendored/bundled** third-party assets (e.g. `file-saver/CHANGELOG.md`), not GSA-authored. Counts as ecosystem presence, not a GSA decision. |

---

## 2. Non-profits / foundations

| Entity | Use / Recommend / Both | Evidence URL | Date | Confidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Apache Software Foundation** | **Use** | https://github.com/apache/iceberg-rust/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Likely | 19 header hits across the `apache` org (iceberg-rust, opendal, cloudstack plugins…). Multiple independent ASF projects; per-project, not a foundation-wide mandate. |
| **CNCF (Cloud Native Computing Foundation)** | **Use** | https://github.com/cncf/landscape2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | *"The format is based on [Keep a Changelog]…"* in CNCF's own `landscape2` tool. Also `contribcard`, `open-community-groups`. 3 hits in the `cncf` org. |
| **OWASP** | **Use** | https://github.com/OWASP/pytm/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | *"The format is based on [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0]…"* in OWASP `pytm`. 13 hits across `OWASP`. (Note: OWASP **MASTG** keeps a changelog but does **not** carry the header — see Debunked.) |
| **Wikimedia Foundation** | **Both** | https://github.com/wikimedia/less.php/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md | 2026-06-06 | Exact | CONTRIBUTING: *"Edit your new section by following the [Keep a changelog] conventions…"*. 52 code hits across `wikimedia` — the largest non-profit footprint found. |
| **Mozilla** | **Use** | https://github.com/mozilla/readability/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md | 2026-06-06 | Likely | 7–8 header hits across `mozilla` (readability, firefox-devtools-mcp, agithub…). Per-project; no org-wide Mozilla recommendation found. |
| **GNOME** | **Use (weak)** | https://github.com/GNOME/snapshot | 2026-06-06 | Likely | 2 hits; partly in sub-crates/patches. Thin evidence. |

## Strongest, most citable picks (shortlist for the References section)

Cleanest evidence, recognizable names, distributed across sectors:

1. **The National Archives (UK)** — *Recommend.* Engineering handbook mandates it: *"Changelogs MUST use the keep a changelog standard."* (handbook-level, org-wide). [link](https://github.com/nationalarchives/engineering-handbook/blob/main/docs/ways-of-working/version-control.md)
2. **Microsoft** — *Use/Both.* 229 repos carry the header; MSTest/testfx among them. [link](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md)
3. **NASA** — *Recommend.* Cumulus CONTRIBUTING: *"The format should follow this standard"* → keepachangelog.com. [link](https://github.com/nasa/cumulus/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
4. **CMS / CMSgov (U.S.)** — *Recommend.* CONTRIBUTING points contributors to keepachangelog.com across multiple repos. [link](https://github.com/CMSgov/bcda-app/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
5. **Wikimedia Foundation** — *Recommend.* CONTRIBUTING: *"follow the Keep a changelog conventions"*; 52 code hits. [link](https://github.com/wikimedia/less.php/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
6. **Google** — *Use.* `google/brotli` carries the header. [link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/brotli/master/CHANGELOG.md)
7. **Cloudflare** — *Use.* `cloudflare/boringtun` carries the header. [link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/boringtun/master/CHANGELOG.md)
8. **CNCF** — *Use.* CNCF's own `landscape2` tool carries the header. [link](https://github.com/cncf/landscape2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
9. **OWASP** — *Use.* `OWASP/pytm` carries the header. [link](https://github.com/OWASP/pytm/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
10. **Textualize (Rich/Textual)** — *Use.* Two high-star CLI/TUI projects, header re-confirmed. [link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Textualize/rich/master/CHANGELOG.md)

**Editorial note:** the two *Recommend-in-documentation* picks worth leading with
are **The National Archives** (a public-sector handbook that *mandates* KAC) and
**Wikimedia/NASA/CMS** CONTRIBUTING files — those are exactly the "an org tells
people to follow it" evidence the section wants, stronger than any single
CHANGELOG.

**Re-verified 2026-06-07 (release day):** all ten shortlist URLs re-fetched live
(HTTP 200), each still carrying its KAC reference. The 2.0 References section now
names five of them, leading with institutions over brands — **NASA**, the **UK's
National Archives**, the **Wikimedia Foundation**, **Cloudflare**, and **Unity** —
without deep links (third-party file paths rot, per the page's own `#linking`
guidance). Microsoft and Google are verified adopters (tables above) but were left
unnamed on the page, to keep the list short and framed as social proof rather than
a brag; the evidence URLs here are the audit trail. Re-verify before any future
republish.

### Cross-check of an external (Gemini) list, 2026-06-07

Every URL resolved and every page *mentioned* KAC, but most claims were
overstated — fetched and assessed each:

- **Unity** — ✅ confirmed. `docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.services.core@1.4`
  changelog: *"The format is based on Keep a Changelog…"* Recognizable, legit USE.
  **Added to the page.**
- **Microsoft** — ✅ confirmed (already cited). `azure-databases-aspire` and
  `vscode-python-devicesimulator` quotes are verbatim-accurate.
- **Storybook** — ⚠️ overstated. Only `storybookjs/addon-designs` (a peripheral
  addon) carries the header; the flagship `storybookjs/storybook` CHANGELOG does
  **not**. Not cited.
- **GovFresh** — ❌ not an adopter. `govfresh.com` is a publication; the page is an
  article *quoting* KAC's old "Who" text, not a government org adopting it.
- **W3C Web Sustainability Guidelines** — ⚠️ a W3C **Community Group** draft lists
  KAC as a *resource* (with SemVer/USWDS), not a W3C Recommendation. Real but not
  a "W3C standard"; not cited to avoid implying standards-body endorsement.
- **GitLab** — ❌ false framing. release-cli issue #81 is an **open feature request
  by a community member**, not GitLab adopting/recommending KAC. Consistent with
  the earlier debunk (GitLab uses git-trailer tooling).

## Could not verify

- **GitLab recommending KAC.** No GitLab handbook/engineering-docs recommendation
  found; `keepachangelog` returns 0 in `gitlab-org`. GitLab uses git-trailer
  changelog generation. Do **not** claim a GitLab endorsement. *(Consistent with
  the aggregate research file.)*
- **GOV.UK / alphagov org-wide recommendation.** alphagov repos use their **own**
  changelog conventions (govuk-frontend, govuk_publishing_components), not KAC.
  `keepachangelog` returns 0 in `alphagov`. No GOV.UK style-guide recommendation
  found. (The UK public-sector signal that *did* hold up is **The National
  Archives**, a separate org.)
- **18F, Red Hat, Canada (canada-ca), EU (ec-europa), FreeBSD.** 0 header hits at
  observation time. Code search indexes a subset, so this is "not found," not
  "proven absent."
- **NIST (usnistgov), U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs.** Code-search hits exist but
  the specific header lines were not individually re-fetched → **Likely**, not
  Exact. Re-fetch the cited files before citing as Exact.
- **GSA (U.S.) as an adopter.** The 2 hits are in **vendored** third-party assets,
  not GSA-authored changelogs. Do not cite GSA as a decision-maker.

## Debunked / no evidence (commonly assumed, but the header isn't there)

These widely-used projects were checked live on 2026-06-06 and their `CHANGELOG.md`
does **not** carry the keepachangelog.com header (most use a different filename,
bespoke notes, or auto-generated release notes):

- **Web/JS:** Vue (`vuejs/vue`), Babel, Prettier, Axios, Bootstrap, SWR, Oh My Zsh, Yarn (berry).
- **Python:** Requests, Click, Poetry, Black, tqdm, Pillow, pre-commit, Astropy, scikit-learn, pydantic, FastAPI.
- **Infra/apps:** Deno, Elasticsearch, Grafana, Home Assistant, Supabase, PostHog, Novu, spotless, lazy.nvim.
- **OWASP MASTG** — keeps a changelog and loosely uses the categories, but the
  file carries **no** keepachangelog.com reference. (OWASP *pytm* does — cite that
  instead.)
- **GitLab** — own git-trailer changelog tooling; no KAC reference.

Takeaway: for marquee standalone OSS the credible story is the **aggregate**
(20,640+ files), plus the handful of genuinely-confirmed names (Textualize, encode).
Don't assert a big project uses KAC without fetching its actual changelog first.

---

## Reproduce

```sh
# Header count inside an org (lower bound; code search indexes a subset):
gh api -X GET search/code \
  -f q='"based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com" org:microsoft' \
  --jq '.total_count'

# Any keepachangelog reference (catches CONTRIBUTING/handbook recommendations):
gh api -X GET search/code -f q='keepachangelog org:wikimedia' --jq '.total_count'

# Then WebFetch the .items[].html_url (raw form) and read the actual line.
```

GitHub's REST search rate limit is low (~10 req/min for code search); space calls
out by ~6s or you'll get HTTP 403 rate-limit responses.

---

# Keep a Changelog 2.0.0 — what changed since 1.1.0

Source: https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog/blob/main/docs/2.0.0-changes.md

# Keep a Changelog 2.0.0 — what changed since 1.1.0

The detailed record of what changed between the 1.1.0 and 2.0.0 pages. The
2.0.0 entry in `CHANGELOG.md` is a synthesized, curated version of this document —
this is the long form for reviewers and translators.

## The most important thing first

**Nothing you have already written becomes invalid.** 2.0.0 adds guidance and
clarifies wording; it does not change the format. Unchanged:

- the six change types — `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`,
  `Security`;
- the `YYYY-MM-DD` date format and the `## [version] - date` heading;
- `[Unreleased]` and `[YANKED]`;
- reverse-chronological order and links to versions and sections.

There is no migration to perform on your changelog. This is an _upgrade guide_ in
the sense of "what's new to know," not "what you must change."

## The big change: from FAQ to integrated guidance

1.1.0 was a short intro followed by a long **Frequently Asked Questions** list.
2.0.0 keeps the friendly opening (`#what`, `#why`, `#who`) but turns the advice
into a structured guide:

- **`#how` — How do I keep a good changelog?** now holds the core guidance as
  named subsections instead of scattered Q&A: `#principles`, `#types`,
  `#breaking`, `#releasing`, `#curation`, plus the questions common enough to
  count as core — `#filename`, `#header` (the `# Changelog` preamble), and
  `#release-notes`. Several of these absorbed adopter-driven conventions: CVE-first
  Security entries and the "keep to the six types" stance (`#types`), inline-vs-
  linked upgrade notes (`#breaking`), the `[version]` compare-link footer
  (`#releasing`), and how to derive release notes without duplicate work
  (`#release-notes`).
- **`#bad-practices` — What makes a changelog worse?** keeps the antipattern list.
- **`#automation` — Changelogs, automation, and LLMs** is a new top-level section
  for the questions a decade of CI/CD and language models raised.
- **`#less-common` — Less common questions** (renamed from "Miscellaneous") and
  **`#about`** collect the situational questions: yanked releases, rewriting,
  large files, monorepos, linking; then standard, scope, contributing.
- **`#references`** replaces the personal "Conversations" footer.

The `#frequently-asked-questions` wrapper heading is gone, along with its first-
person framing. The voice is now plainer and less about the author — see
`docs/tone-and-voice.md` for the guide that drives this.

## The tagline changed

The signature line is new in 2.0.0:

- **Was:** "Don't let your friends dump git logs into changelogs."
- **Now:** "Clearly document the evolution of your projects."

It drives the hero subtitle and the page's meta/Open Graph description, so
translators should translate the _new_ line. The old one was git-centric and
leaned on an English idiom; the new one is active, leads with clarity, and is
plainer to translate. Older versions keep the original tagline.

## At a glance

- **9 new sections** of guidance: `#breaking`, `#curation`, `#automation`,
  `#release-notes`, `#large-changelog`, `#monorepos`, `#linking`, `#scope`,
  `#references`.
- **Core advice restructured** from a flat FAQ into `#how` subsections.
- **Several sections revised** in wording (mostly clarifications held back from
  minor releases — see the 2.0.0 changelog entry for why).
- **`#effort` and `#confusing-dates` folded** into `#releasing`.
- **`#github-releases` generalized** to `#release-notes` (any host, not just
  GitHub).
- **Content removed**: the Vandamme gem reference, the "Can changelogs be
  automatically parsed?" framing, the "help me collect antipatterns" aside, and
  the personal podcast footer (kept, synthesized, in `#references`).

## New guidance

### Working with the change types

- **`#types` expanded.** Beyond the six-type list, it now resolves the boundary
  people ask about most — `Fixed` vs `Changed` vs `Security` — with a "was the old
  behavior a bug?" test, an **aside** on why there aren't more types (the reason
  for a change belongs in the entry's wording, not a new type), and direct answers
  for **Dependencies** and **Known issues**.
- **`#breaking` — marking breaking changes (new).** A `**Breaking:**` marker on
  `Changed` / `Removed` entries rather than a new section, plus: name which
  interface your versioning scheme treats as stable.

### Versioning and release structure

- **`#releasing` — Structuring a release (was `#effort`).** Keeps the `Unreleased`
  guidance, absorbs the date-format rationale from the old `#confusing-dates`, adds
  the optional **per-release summary**, and adds that you don't have to use
  Semantic Versioning — CalVer, a plain number, or a date are fine, and
  continuously deployed projects can keep dated entries under `Unreleased`. Now
  also explains the **`[version]` reference-link footer** (resolve each version to
  a `compare/…` URL): this is how a plain changelog provides the tag association
  and "what changed" diff a hosted release page gives you, on any host. `#linking`
  reinforces the same reference-link pattern for issue/PR/commit refs.
- **`#curation` — Curate, don't accumulate (new).** Names the discipline at the heart of
  the project: a changelog records _notable_ changes, and deciding which is which
  is human work. Contains the **aside** clarifying that "don't dump git logs" does
  not mean "sort every commit into a type as you make it."

### Automation and the LLM era

- **`#automation` — Changelogs, automation, and LLMs (new).** One section covering:
  - **no separate machine format** — a consistent changelog is parseable _because_
    it was written for people; "this page is the format";
  - **LLM-drafted changelogs** — "machines can draft, but humans curate"; the new
    failure mode is a fluent changelog no one read; includes a portable brief to
    drop into an **`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`** (itself an aside);
  - **Conventional Commits and generators** (semantic-release, release-please,
    Changesets, git-cliff) — a commit and a changelog entry are written for
    different readers and don't convert cleanly into each other; type-filtering
    shortens the list but doesn't make that shift; a generated changelog is raw
    material a person still has to curate;
  - **CI/CD** — let it do the mechanics (release-time `Unreleased`→version move,
    format checks, gentle reminders); don't hard-gate every change.

### Maintaining a changelog over time

- **`#release-notes` — changelog vs release notes (new, generalizes
  `#github-releases`).** Different audiences and homes; derive release notes from
  the changelog. Names host release systems (GitHub Releases, GitLab Releases) and
  makes the portability/lock-in case explicit: their notes live in one platform's
  database, don't travel with `git clone`, and are stranded if you change or leave
  the host. Recommends `CHANGELOG.md` as the canonical record that carries the same
  data, with the host's release pages generated from it.
- **`#large-changelog` — very large changelogs (new).** One file is usually fine;
  if you split, archive only stable-old versions and link both ways. Don't prune.
- **`#monorepos` — monorepos (new).** Unrelated projects → independent changelogs;
  a unified product → per-component changelogs _plus_ a central one.
- **`#linking` — linking to issues or pull requests (new).** Reasonable and at your
  discretion, but URLs 404 when repos move and PR/MR numbers aren't portable; git
  tags and commit refs are repo-canonical.

### Scope and framing

- **`#scope` — what Keep a Changelog won't do (new).** The non-goals: no growing the
  type set, no machine format/schema/required layout, no becoming a tool or runtime,
  no single-vendor lock-in.
- **`#references` (new).** Replaces the first-person "Conversations" footer with a
  short, synthesized note: how the convention grew (with a link to its own
  changelog) and the podcast, the convention's reach (languages and project count),
  named adopters (NASA, the UK's National Archives, the Wikimedia Foundation,
  Cloudflare, Unity), and its research citations. Written to be easy to translate.

## Revised sections

| Section                 | What changed                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `#what`                 | A changelog is a "curated, chronologically ordered list" (tightened from 1.1.0's wording).                                                 |
| `#why`                  | Plainer phrasing; "notable changes between each version."                                                                                  |
| `#who`                  | Plainer phrasing; less idiom.                                                                                                              |
| `#principles`           | Generalized "Semantic Versioning" to "versioning scheme," and added a principle: **write plainly — many readers are not native speakers.** |
| `#log-diffs`            | Adds the **git-log definition** as a blockquote (what a "git log" is and that this applies to any version control system, not just git).   |
| `#inconsistent-changes` | Plainer wording; the old "help collect antipatterns" aside is dropped.                                                                     |
| `#standard`             | Reframed as historical and humbler — KAC doesn't aim to be the one true standard; broadened to any project communicating changes.          |
| `#filename`             | Adds the rebuttal to "a changelog should list _all_ changes" (version control already does that).                                          |
| `#yanked`               | Plainer wording; same guidance.                                                                                                            |
| `#rewrite`              | Adds: note the date you updated an entry after release.                                                                                    |
| `#contribute`           | Humbler, less first-person; "one carefully considered opinion."                                                                            |

## Merged / renamed / removed

**Merged**

- `#effort` ("How can I reduce the effort…") → folded into `#releasing`.
- `#confusing-dates` → date rationale folded into `#releasing`.

**Renamed / generalized**

- `#bad-practices` heading "Can changelogs be bad?" → "What makes a changelog
  worse?"
- `#github-releases` ("What about GitHub Releases?") → `#release-notes`, broadened
  beyond GitHub.

**Removed**

- `#automatic` ("Can changelogs be automatically parsed?") and its **Vandamme**
  (Ruby gem) reference — superseded by `#automation`.
- The `#frequently-asked-questions` wrapper heading.
- The "help me collect antipatterns" aside (open an issue).
- The personal "Conversations" footer — synthesized into `#references`.

## Presentation changes (for maintainers of this site, not translators)

These don't affect the content's meaning but are part of the 2.0 release:

- **English 2.0.0 is authored in Markdown** (`source/en/2.0.0/index.html.md`)
  instead of HAML, with stable `{#id}` anchors — easier for contributors and
  closer to a real changelog. Other languages and older versions stay HAML for now
  (see Translation impact). Links use **reference style**, with every URL collected
  in one block at the bottom of the file, so the prose stays readable and the link
  list is easy to audit and translate. Fenced code examples use ` ```backticks ```;
kramdown's GFM parser is enabled for this (its native fence is `~~~`).
- **New stylesheet `v2.css`** — native modern CSS, no framework or preprocessor;
  the brand palette in oklch; logical properties for RTL.
- **Light and dark themes** via `light-dark()` and `color-scheme`, with a header
  switch (`system` / `light` / `dark`). System follows the OS; an explicit choice
  persists in `localStorage` and is applied before first paint to avoid a flash.
- **A table-of-contents sidebar** built in JS from the page's top-level headings
  (the intro cards are excluded, so it lists the real sections): sticky in the
  left gutter on wide screens (with scroll-spy highlighting and a second breakpoint
  that widens it), collapsing to an "On this page" menu on narrow ones that
  dismisses once a section is chosen.
- **A centered "Changelog basics" heading titles the What / Why / Who intro**,
  shown as a card triptych (titles: _What is it?_ / _Why keep one?_ /
  _Who needs this?_) — a row on wide screens, stacked on narrow.
- **The example changelog collapses** to a tap-to-open disclosure on narrow
  screens and shows outright on wide ones.
- **Heading anchor links** — a `#` revealed on hover/focus to grab a section link.
- **The header keeps to one row on narrow screens** — the language picker collapses
  behind its globe icon below 30rem and reveals the selector when tapped (with
  `aria-expanded`, Escape/outside-click to close); at wider widths the selector
  shows inline as before. Below 30rem the brand mark also moves from the hero into
  the header (before the picker), so it doesn't crowd the title; while the picker
  is open the header grows so the revealed select rests on it, not over the hero.
- **A pinned header after the hero** — once the hero scrolls out of view a small
  IntersectionObserver pins the header to the top (above the narrow breakpoint),
  so the language and theme controls and the brand mark stay reachable while
  reading; the mark gains a "Keep a Changelog" wordmark beside it at >=48rem. The
  header leaves flow when pinned, with matching padding to avoid a scroll jump and
  a scroll offset so anchored jumps clear it.
- **The brand mark follows the accent** — ocre in light, gold in dark (a branded
  palette color rather than plain cream), and optically centered with the wordmark.
- **Content lists are indented** with hanging markers so they stand apart from the
  prose; **the version marker** reads at body size with tightened spacing before
  the first section.
- **The "On this page" toggle stacks below the version** until ~600px (it doesn't
  share a row with the long "Version … Published on …" line in a thin gutter).
- **Mobile hardening** — long code lines no longer stretch the page (the reading
  column shrinks and code blocks scroll); the hero pattern is anchored at the top
  so revealing the example changelog extends it rather than shifting it; inline
  code carries a hairline border so it reads on any surface (including asides).
- **The topographic hero pattern and the tree-ring logomark are restored**; the
  pattern is rendered as accessible light contour lines over the deep-ocre base,
  and the brand mark is a theme-colored silhouette that reads in light and dark.
- **Asides vs blockquotes are now visually distinct** — asides are filled callouts
  with an ocre rule (step-aside notes); blockquotes are italic with a gold rule
  (definitions and citations).
- **Accessibility** — the 2.0 design meets WCAG 2.1 AA (verified with axe-core in
  light and dark, including the theme switch, TOC, and hero).

## Translation impact

**Translations are not being converted to Markdown.** Existing language files stay
in HAML, and older versions are untouched. For 2.0.0, the goal is **new
translations authored from the 1.1.0 baseline up to the English 2.0.0** — translate
the new and revised content rather than porting file formats.

- The English `source/en/2.0.0/index.html.md` is the reference for new 2.0
  translations.
- Per `ruby translation_coverage.rb --migration`, each existing translation needs
  the new sections added and the revised sections updated to reach 2.0.0; unchanged
  sections carry over. Run `--migration --details` for the per-language,
  per-section breakdown.
- Section ids are stable across languages, so a 2.0 translation should match the
  English id set: `#basics`, `#what`, `#why`, `#who`, `#how`, `#principles`, `#types`,
  `#breaking`, `#releasing`, `#curation`, `#filename`, `#header`,
  `#release-notes`, `#bad-practices`, `#log-diffs`, `#ignoring-deprecations`,
  `#inconsistent-changes`, `#automation`, `#less-common`, `#yanked`, `#rewrite`,
  `#large-changelog`, `#monorepos`, `#linking`, `#credits`, `#about`, `#standard`,
  `#scope`, `#contribute`, `#references`.

---

# Keep a Changelog — Verified Citations

Source: https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog/blob/main/docs/2.0.0-citations.md

# Keep a Changelog — Verified Citations

## Method and caveats

This document records a skeptical, source-by-source verification of a list of
claimed citations of **Keep a Changelog** (KAC, <https://keepachangelog.com>).
The original list was generated by an LLM (Gemini), which is known to fabricate
academic citations, DOIs, author lists, and the very claim that a source cites
KAC. **Nothing below is taken on the list's word.** A claim is marked
**VERIFIED** only when the actual source was fetched (or a faithful
open-access copy: arXiv preprint, author's institutional PDF, publisher HTML)
and a real reference to "Keep a Changelog" or `keepachangelog.com` was found in
the body text, a footnote, or the bibliography — captured as an exact quote.

- **Access date:** all sources fetched and checked on **2026-06-07**.
- **Staleness caveat:** web pages (industry blogs, The Turing Way, HMC's
  hosted PDF) can change or move after this date. URLs that resolved on the
  access date may rot. Paper DOIs are stable; the open-access PDFs used to read
  full text may move.
- **Open-access substitution caveat:** for paywalled papers (IEEE, ACM) the KAC
  reference was confirmed in the open preprint / author PDF, which is the same
  manuscript but may differ in pagination and reference numbering from the
  final published version of record.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Ref [6]: "Keep a Changelog. https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/ (accessed December 12, 2022)." Conventional Commits is the next reference, matching the "alongside Conventional Commits" claim. | **VERIFIED** | DOI casing in claim was `hmc_publ_04`; actual is **HMC_publ_04** (case only). | Doc Holiday, *How to Write Release Notes From Commit Messages* | Industry blog | <https://doc.holiday/blog/how-to-write-release-notes-from-commit-messages> | **Yes** (body, named + linked) | "Keep a Changelog puts it plainly: 'commit log diffs as changelogs is a bad idea: they're full of noise.'" Uses the KAC category set as claimed. |
| DEV Community, *Keep a changelog!* by Marco Ieni | Industry blog | <https://dev.to/marcoieni/keep-a-changelog-hf0> | **Yes** (body) | "After some online research I found this really nice website called, in fact, keep a changelog." Describes adopting the Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security format plus SemVer for the intellimacs project. | **VERIFIED** | Author and adoption narrative confirmed. |

## Verified, citable

These eight sources were read in full text (or faithful open-access copy) and
contain a genuine, quotable reference to Keep a Changelog. They are safe to
list in a public References section.

**Peer-reviewed / institutional (strongest):**

1. **Ochoa, Degueule, Falleri & Vinju (2022)** — *BreakBot* (ICSE-NIER),
   DOI 10.1145/3510455.3512783. Bibliography entry: "Olivier Lacan. 2019. Keep
   a ChangeLog. https://keepachangelog.com".
2. **Imtiaz, Khanom & Williams (2022)** — *Open or Sneaky?* (IEEE TSE),
   DOI 10.1109/TSE.2022.3181010. Bibliography entry: "keep a changelog,
   https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/".
3. **Hertz & McNeill (2024)** — *Eleven quick tips for properly handling
   tabular data* (PLOS Comput Biol), DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012604. Cited in
   Tip 9 and reference [33].
4. **The Turing Way** — Project Documentation page links to and recommends
   keepachangelog.com.
5. **Helmholtz Metadata Collaboration (2022)** — *Guidance on Versioning of
   Digital Assets*, DOI 10.3289/HMC_publ_04. Cites keepachangelog.com (ref [6])
   alongside Conventional Commits.

**Industry blogs:**

6. **Doc Holiday** — names and directly quotes Keep a Changelog.
7. **CloudBees** — recommends the keepachangelog.com standard and its category set.
8. **DEV Community / Marco Ieni** — narrates adopting the KAC format.

## Could not confirm

None. Every source on the list was reachable and its full text or references
were inspected on 2026-06-07. (No sources are left in
"EXISTS, KAC-CITATION UNCONFIRMED.")

## Debunked

- **Venturini, Cogo, Polato, Gerosa & Wiese (2023)**, *I depended on you and
  you broke me* (ACM TOSEM, DOI 10.1145/3576037). The paper is real and the
  authors/title/DOI are correct, **but it does not cite the Keep a Changelog
  standard or keepachangelog.com.** It only recommends maintaining a changelog
  as a general good practice and uses "changelog" / "keep a changelog" as
  generic terms. There is no `keepachangelog` string and no KAC bibliography
  entry anywhere in the manuscript. Gemini's claim that it cites "the KAC
  standard" is fabricated. **Do not cite this as a KAC reference.**

## Author/metadata corrections caught

- **BreakBot:** Gemini listed three authors; the paper has **four** (added
  Jurgen Vinju). Correct arXiv ID is **2111.05132**.
- **HMC:** correct DOI casing is **10.3289/HMC_publ_04**; ten authors, first is
  Pier Luigi Buttigieg.
- **Turing Way:** Gemini's page slug was wrong (404). Real page is
  `reproducible-research/code-documentation/code-documentation-project`.
- **CloudBees:** live URL slug is misspelled `appy-...` on CloudBees' side.
- **Doc Holiday:** domain is `doc.holiday` (no `www`).

# Keep a Changelog — history claims, verified

Source: https://github.com/olivierlacan/keep-a-changelog/blob/main/docs/2.0.0-history.md

# Keep a Changelog — history claims, verified

Fact-check of a Gemini-generated "history of Keep a Changelog" before deciding
whether any of it belongs in the 2.0.0 release. Gemini fabricates and overstates,
so every factual claim here was checked against a primary source, and claims that
conflict with the project's settled editorial positions are flagged.

**Verified: 2026-06-07.** Method: this repo's `CHANGELOG.md`, `config.rb`, git
tags, and the GitHub REST API for repo facts; the live `keepachangelog.com` spec
for wording; the actual WP Tavern article; npm/crates registries for tooling
dates; web search for the Linux Foundation / CNCF and Linear/Beamer claims.
Confirmed adoption facts are reused from `docs/2.0.0-adoption-research.md` and
`docs/2.0.0-adoption-sectors.md` rather than re-verified.

Statuses: **VERIFIED** (primary source confirms), **UNVERIFIED** (could not
confirm), **DEBUNKED** (false/overstated), **CONFLICT** (contradicts a settled
project position).

---

## Verified timeline (only what holds up)

Each line has a primary source and a date.

- **2014-05-31 — Repository created by Olivier Lacan.** GitHub API
  `created_at: 2014-05-31T05:23:54Z`, `owner: olivierlacan`; matches this repo's
  `CHANGELOG.md` `[0.0.1] - 2014-05-31` and `docs/2.0.0-adoption-research.md`
  ("Repo created 2014-05-31"). The 0.0.1 entry: *"This CHANGELOG file to hopefully
  serve as an evolving example of a standardized open source project CHANGELOG."*
- **2015-02-16 — First notable press coverage (WP Tavern), by Sarah Gooding.**
  Title: *"Keep a CHANGELOG Project Aims to Standardize Best Practices for Writing
  Change Logs."* Describes "a site and corresponding GitHub repository" created by
  Olivier Lacan, "a software engineer at Code School," offering "an extensive
  collection of recommendations for writing better change logs."
- **2017-06-20 — v1.0.0 released.** `CHANGELOG.md` `[1.0.0] - 2017-06-20`;
  confirmed by git tag `v1.0.0`. This release added the Why/Who/How and Guiding
  Principles sections and a large batch of translations.
- **2019-02-15 — v1.1.0 released.** `CHANGELOG.md` `[1.1.0] - 2019-02-15`; tag
  `v1.1.0`.
- **2023-03-05 — v1.1.1 released.** `CHANGELOG.md` `[1.1.1] - 2023-03-05`; tag
  `v1.1.1`. (CHANGELOG notes "26 translations to date" at this point.)
- **Core principle — "Changelogs are for humans, not machines."** Live spec at
  keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0 lists it verbatim as a Guiding Principle. (The
  Guiding Principles section was introduced in v1.0.0, 2017.)
- **Six change types — Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security.**
  Confirmed verbatim and in this order on the live 1.1.0 spec. The 2.0.0
  CHANGELOG entry explicitly keeps them unchanged.
- **28 translations.** `config.rb` `$languages` / `$language_count` = 28 (primary,
  in-tree); see `docs/2.0.0-adoption-research.md`.

---

## Claim-by-claim table

| # | Gemini claim | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | KAC originated in **2014**, founded by **Olivier Lacan** | **VERIFIED** | GitHub API `created_at` 2014-05-31; `owner: olivierlacan`; `CHANGELOG.md` `[0.0.1] - 2014-05-31`. |
| 2 | Core line **"Changelogs are for humans, not machines"** | **VERIFIED** | Live 1.1.0 spec: *"Changelogs are for humans, not machines."* Listed as a Guiding Principle (section added in v1.0.0, 2017). |
| 3 | **v1.0.0 in 2017** with **six change types** (Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security) | **VERIFIED** | `CHANGELOG.md` `[1.0.0] - 2017-06-20`; tag `v1.0.0`; six types confirmed verbatim on live spec. |
| 4 | **2015 virality / "WP Tavern, February 2015" coverage** | **VERIFIED** | Article exists, dated **2015-02-16**, by Sarah Gooding. Confirms a real, dated 2015 article. ("Virality" itself is not quantified by the source — the article is the verifiable fact.) |
| 5 | Translated into **"over 30 languages"** | **CONFLICT / DEBUNKED** | Primary source `config.rb` `$language_count` = **28**, not 30+. See position 3 below. |
| 6 | KAC is a **"Manifesto"** (Gemini section title) | **CONFLICT** | Framing conflict — see position 1 below. |
| 7 | **Conventional Commits / git-cliff are "complementary"** ("the structure of KAC without the manual labor") | **CONFLICT** | Contradicts the project's codified stance — see position 2 below. |

Dates hold; the "complementary" framing does not (see #7). |
